title: Working at Redwood: Roles, Career Ladders, Benefits, Hiring & Onboarding, and Internal Tools
author: Aisha Kumar
summary: Comprehensive company handbook section describing life at Redwood: values and ways of working, role families and career ladders, benefits and perks, hiring and onboarding flow, and practical guides to core internal tools.
content:
Purpose and scope

This page provides a single reference for engineers, product managers, and new hires to understand how we work at Redwood, the structure of role families and career ladders, the benefits and perks we offer, our hiring and onboarding flow, and the primary internal tools new and existing employees should know. Use this as a living document; People Ops owns updates and works with each team to keep role ladders and benefits current.

1) Working at Redwood — mission, values, and ways of working

Intro: Redwood Inference is a developer-first platform focused on production-grade LLM inference. Our mission and technical priorities shape how we hire, decide, and collaborate.

Core values (one-line and examples):
- Be productive first: prioritize shipping reliable, well-tested features; prefer incremental improvements with clear ownership.
- User-centric engineering: measure decisions by developer and customer impact (latency, cost, reliability).
- Operational humility: design for observable, debuggable systems and automate toil away.
- Radical clarity: document architecture, APIs, and runbooks so any team can operate services in production.
- Inclusive collaboration: recruit diverse perspectives and commit to respectful, evidence-based debates.

Ways of working (team norms):
- Async-first communication: document decisions in Confluence, prefer asynchronous updates, and use short, scheduled syncs for alignment.
- PR-level ownership: PRs should include a short summary, testing plan, and rollback criteria.
- On-call shared responsibility: teams share on-call rotations and maintain runbooks under eng-sre.
- Quarterly planning: teams publish priorities and OKRs in product-docs/roadmap-and-themes.

2) Role families and career ladders (overview)

This section summarizes role families and promotion principles. Each role family has a separate ladder page (links in Related Pages). Promotions are competency-based and rely on evidence: impact, scope, influence, technical depth, and leadership. Performance cycles and promotion ramps are handled by People Ops and engineering managers.

Role families covered here: engineering, research & applied ML, product & design, people-ops, customer-success, finance & legal, go-to-market.

Common promotion principles:
- Outcomes over outputs: candidates must show sustained impact across multiple quarters.
- Breadth and depth: senior levels require cross-team influence and architectural ownership.
- Evidence-based: promotions use dossiers with PRs, design docs, customer feedback, and manager recommendations.
- Calibration: managers present promotion cases in a cross-functional calibration forum.

Example engineering ladder highlights (short):
- IC1 / New Grad: delivers tasks with mentorship, writes tests, and follows engineering standards.
- IC2 / Software Engineer: owns features, contributes to design docs, and reliably completes projects.
- Senior (IC3): leads medium-sized projects, mentors others, drives design reviews, and simplifies operational complexity.
- Staff (IC4): shapes architecture across services, leads cross-team initiatives, and acts as a technical multiplier.
- Principal / Distinguished (IC5+): defines company-wide architecture and strategic technical direction.

Manager tracks: engineering managers and above include people management competency, hiring and retention ownership, and career development. Individual contributor tracks emphasize technical leadership and cross-team influence.

3) Benefits and perks (current plan highlights)

This section summarizes the standard benefits available to full-time employees in North America and Europe. Regional variations may apply; see People Ops for country-specific SOWs.

Health & wellbeing:
- Medical, dental, and vision plans with employer contribution (US & CA: platinum/gold tiers; EU: local provider options).
- Employee Assistance Program (EAP) and mental health sessions covered.

Financial and compensation:
- Competitive base salary, annual performance-based salary review, and incentive/bonus programs where applicable.
- Equity: standard RSU grants with cliff and vesting schedule detailed in offer letters.
- 401(k) / pension guidance and employer matching where regionally applicable.

Time off and leaves:
- Flexible vacation policy with manager alignment; recommended minimum 15 days/year PTO accrual guidance.
- Parental leave: primary & secondary caregiver policies with top-up for eligible employees.
- Sick leave and caregiver leave per local law.

Family & home support:
- Hybrid work allowance for home office equipment and monthly remote-work stipend.
- Relocation assistance for approved hires; visa sponsorship handled by People Ops for qualifying roles.

Learning & development:
- $2,000 annual learning stipend (pro-rated on start date) for training, conferences, and books.
- Dedicated mentorship and 20% learning time guidelines for technical growth.

Perks & culture:
- Monthly team allowance for lunches or co-working days; regular internal tech talks and offsites.
- Commuter benefits where available; travel support for conferences and customer meetings.

How to access benefits (process table):
- Enrollment window: new hires enroll in benefits within 30 days of start date.
- Open enrollment: yearly window in November for most regions.
- Contact People Ops: people-ops@redwood.com for exceptions, accommodations, and country-specific questions.

4) Hiring and onboarding overview

High-level hiring philosophy: hire for mission alignment, technical rigor, and operational excellence. We run structured interviews designed to assess role-specific skills, collaboration style, and ownership mindset.

Interview stages (standard for engineering and product):
1. Recruiter screen: role fit, compensation expectations, and timeline.
2. Hiring manager / technical manager screen: high-level technical fit or product sense.
3. Technical interview loop (2-4 interviews): coding/design/architecture, system design, and culture fit. For applied ML roles, include model analysis and evaluation exercises.
4. Leadership partner / cross-functional interview: alignment with team goals and communication style.
5. Offer & references: People Ops coordinates offer details, equity, and start date.

Interview guides and rubrics: interviewers should use standardized rubrics stored in sales-enablement/positioning-and-messaging to ensure consistent scoring and bias mitigation. Interviewers must complete anti-bias training annually.

Offer & negotiation guidelines:
- People Ops owns the compensation band guidelines and approves exceptions.
- Managers provide role justification and expected impact for the candidate.
- Counter-offers: People Ops will review but managers should avoid open-ended promises.

New hire onboarding (30/60/90 template):
- Day 0-7: HR & security tasks (accounts, OKTA, equipment), team introductions, first-week checklist, and buddy assignment.
- 30 days: contributor-level tasks, small tickets, and initial architecture overviews; manager 1:1s weekly.
- 60 days: increased ownership of feature work, participate in on-call shadowing, and career development conversation.
- 90 days: full project ownership, performance checkpoint, and feedback loop for manager and peer calibration.

Manager onboarding responsibilities (short checklist):
- Prepare onboarding plan and first projects, create access requests (GitHub, CI/CD), schedule 1:1s and team intro, assign buddy and mentor.
- Confirm equipment delivery and software licenses.

5) Internal tools guide (practical quickstart)

This section lists primary internal systems, ownership, common tasks, and links to more detailed guides. For platform and infra-specific runbooks, see eng-infra and eng-platform spaces.

Core systems and quick actions:
- OKTA (identity & SSO): initial SSO login, MFA setup, and application access requests. For app access, open an access request via People Ops or your manager.
- Slack (communication): request private channels, team channels naming conventions, and archived channel policy. Use /rename for ephemeral channels during projects.
- Confluence (documentation): create pages under your team space; use page templates (onboarding, runbook, design doc). All architecture decisions should have an ADR in architecture-and-standards/decision-records.
- GitHub (source control): org membership, repo access requests, branch naming policy, and protected branch rules. Create PRs with templates and link to Jira issue IDs.
- Jira (task tracking): project keys, issue templates, sprint cadence, and triage process. Use labels and components for cross-team visibility.
- CI/CD (build and deploy): short checklist to get access: request pipeline permissions, read deploy runbooks in eng-platform/runbooks, and shadow a release.
- Payroll & HR portal: update tax and bank details, submit expense reports, and request time off.

Access and security notes:
- Least privilege principle: request only the permissions needed for your role and escalate for temporary access.
- Secrets & keys: use the company Key Management Service (KMS) and never commit secrets to GitHub. See security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth for policy.
- VPN / Private deployments: People Ops and Eng-Private-Deployments coordinate access for on-prem customers and restricted networks.

6) Escalations, incident involvement, and runbooks

On-call and incident expectations: all teams participate in on-call rotations appropriate to product impact. New hires should shadow on-call for the first rotation. Maintain runbooks and postmortems in oncall-and-incident-response.

Escalation path (short):
1. Follow the service runbook and check dashboards.
2. Notify primary on-call for the service.
3. If unresolved within the SLA window, escalate to the secondary on-call and team lead.
4. For security incidents, contact Security on-call and People Ops for sensitive personnel actions.

7) How to request changes or raise questions

- Policy changes and handbook updates: submit a PR to this Confluence page (People Ops reviews) or email people-ops@redwood.com. Major policy changes require legal and finance review and a 14-day comment period.
- Role ladder clarifications: speak to your manager; for cross-team calibration, raise the case in the People Ops promotions channel.
- Benefits exceptions: contact People Ops with documentation; all exceptions require manager approval and HR signoff.

Appendix: links and templates
- New hire 30/60/90 template (Confluence page).
- Interview rubric templates (Confluence: sales-enablement/positioning-and-messaging).
- Engineering PR template and design doc checklist (eng-developer-experience/docs-site).
- Runbook template and incident postmortem checklist (/confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/postmortem).

Ownership and maintenance
- Document owner: People Ops (people-ops@redwood.com).
- Review cadence: annual review each January and targeted updates following major policy changes (e.g., benefits, regional laws).
- Publication: Changes will be published and communicated in Slack #announcements and via manager email.

Feedback: If anything here is unclear or missing, file a Confluence comment on this page or contact People Ops directly.
